title: Chemical Markup Language 2011
items.abstract: <jats:p>With the release of Chem4Word (sorry Chemistry Add-in for Word) we've reached an important milestone in the development of CML. CML is about 16 years old (Henry will give a better estimate – but I think we can reasonably date it from our trip to WWW1 and henry's subsequent trip to WWW2). I think it's reasonably come of age and can now be regarded as the de facto approach to representing semantic chemistry.</jats:p>

title: OPSIN and OSCAR – Chemical language processing
items.abstract: <jats:p>This blog is about new developments in our chemical language processors OSCAR and OPSIN and about how OMII (eScience) and we are taking them forward. WE also have a JISC project with NacTEM – CheTA and I'll write more later about that. Many of you will know that we have been interested for several years in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) of chemistry texts.</jats:p>

title: Financial, Statistical Analysis and Investment using Rust Language Programming
Chemical Informatics and China; and challenges of language
items.abstract: <jats:p>I was honoured last week to be invited by Professor Xiaoxia Li to speak at the 14 <sup> th </sup> Asian Chemistry Congress in Bangkok and then to visit her group in Beijing. Unfortunately I couldn't spend longer but the visit impressed me very much, both with the focus of the group and their high morale.</jats:p>
